articles.title: National Education Policy 2024: Reforming Medical Education
articles.content: The National Education Policy 2024 is transforming Indias healthcare and education landscape. It emphasizes skill development, multidisciplinary learning, and research-driven innovation to create a future-ready medical workforce. National Education Policy 2024: The New National Education Policy 2024 (NEP 2024) brings big reform in Indias education and healthcare systems. Approved by the Union Cabinet of India, it is an extension of the NEP 2020 framework to strengthen holistic learning, skill-based education, and research-driven innovation. The New National Education Policy (NEP) 2024 revolutionises Indias education system with a focus on healthcare skill development, multidisciplinary learning, and innovation. It aims to prepare a globally competent workforce by integrating medical, nursing, and AYUSH education, encouraging industry collaboration, and enhancing vocational training for a future-ready healthcare sector. With over 50 of Indias population under 35 years, NEP 2024 sees youth as the nations biggest asset. Indias healthcare education has expanded significantly under NEP 2024: The policy proposes to upgrade 600 district hospitals into teaching hospitals, bridging practical learning with healthcare service delivery. This ensures collaborative healthcare delivery aligned with Indias traditional and modern systems. Read Also: AYUSH vs Allopathy: What Are the Legal  Medical Limits? By bridging medicine, data science, and technology, India can accelerate innovation in medical devices, biotechnology, and Ayurvedic biology. The policy promotes research and innovation hubs that encourage cross-disciplinary collaboration.India aims to reduce dependence on imported medical devices (41,000 crore in 2020) by: This focus positions India as a self-reliant global health innovator. Skill development is the cornerstone of NEP 2024: These initiatives will create a future-ready, skilled healthcare workforce aligned with Indias National Skill Development Mission. The New National Education Policy 2024, part of the NEP 2020 Framework, goes beyond academic reform; its a transformational framework for healthcare and skill empowerment. By integrating education, industry, and innovation, NEP 2024 ensures Indias medical professionals are globally competitive, ethically driven, and socially conscious. With its focus on Education for All, Skills for Life, NEP 2024 is poised to make India a global hub for healthcare innovation and learning excellence. articles.title: Taliban Attacks Pakistani Troops: Escalation at the Border
articles.content: The Taliban government has confirmed its involvement in attacks against Pakistani troops across various mountainous regions along the northern border. The situation escalated as the Taliban described these operations as retaliatory, following claims that Pakistan had violated Afghan airspace and conducted airstrikes on a market within Afghanistans territory on Thursday. The details surrounding the casualties from these attacks remain unclear. Reacting to the Talibans actions, Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi condemned the assaults as unprovoked and accused the Taliban of targeting civilians. He warned that Pakistani forces would respond decisively, stating, We will respond with a stone for every brick. This statement underscores the heightened tensions between the two nations, with Islamabad accusing Kabul of providing a safe haven for terrorists who conduct operations against Pakistan. The escalating conflict comes amid a historic visit by Afghan Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi to India. Reports indicate that both sides have utilized small arms and artillery in the Kunar-Kurram region, contributing to the ongoing violence. Minister Naqvi strongly condemned the Talibans actions, labeling the firing by Afghan forces at civilian areas as a blatant violation of international laws. He described Afghanistans actions as a game of fire and blood in a post shared on X (formerly Twitter). A Pakistani military spokesman indicated that necessary measures would be implemented to protect Pakistani lives and property. Although the military has not made an official statement, a security source revealed to the BBC that firing was reported at several locations along the Pakistani-Afghan border, including Angoor Adda, Bajaur, Kurram, Dir, Chitral, and Baramcha. A police official stationed near the Zero Point in Kurram district reported heavy weapons fire originating from the Afghan side at around 22:00 local time (17:00 GMT), with intense gunfire reported from multiple border locations. Last week, the Taliban government accused Pakistan of violating its sovereign territory, coinciding with two loud blasts heard late Thursday in Kabul. The Taliban Defence Ministry claimed that Pakistan had bombed a civilian market in Paktika, a province located in southeastern Afghanistan, stating that numerous shops were destroyed as a result. In response, a senior Pakistani general alleged that Afghanistan was being used as a base for terrorist operations against Pakistan. Pakistan has long accused the Afghan Taliban of allowing the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) to operate from Afghan soil, launching attacks against the Islamabad government in pursuit of imposing a strict Islamic governance system. The Taliban government, however, has consistently denied these allegations. The latest surge in hostilities coincides with the Afghan Taliban Foreign Ministers visit to India. During this diplomatic thaw, India announced plans to reopen its embassy in Kabul, which had been closed since the Talibans return to power four years ago. Minister Naqvi further warned that Afghanistan would face consequences akin to those faced by India if it continued its hostile posture towards Pakistan. In light of the escalating tensions, Saudi Arabia, which recently signed a mutual defense pact with Pakistan, has called for restraint and urged both Islamabad and Kabul to avoid further escalation. Similarly, Qatar expressed concern regarding the border tensions and emphasized the importance of dialogue, diplomacy, and restraint between the two nations. articles.title: OP Rajbhar Demands Seats, Threatens to Contest Bihar Elections ...
articles.content: Amid Bihar Assembly election preparations, NDA ally OP Rajbhar has demanded a share of seats for his party. Sources report that Rajbhar has made it clear he will contest independently if the seat-sharing demands are not met. This announcement has added fresh tension within the NDA alliance as discussions over constituency allocation continue. Analysts suggest that Rajbhars move could impact NDAs overall strategy, especially in areas where his party has a significant voter base. The development highlights ongoing negotiations and potential fractures within the coalition as parties work to finalize their seat-sharing formulas ahead of the polls. articles.content: This bulletin highlights the controversy surrounding Afghanistans Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi, who is set to visit the Taj Mahal in Agra after recently barring women journalists from his press conference at the Afghan embassy in New Delhi. Opposition parties have criticised the government for allowing a foreign fundamentalist to dictate terms on Indian soil and also insulting Indian women journalists. The Ministry of External Affairs responded, clarifying that the press interaction took place entirely within the Afghan embassys premises and that the Indian government had no role in the decision. The episode has ignited a debate on diplomatic protocol and womens rights.
